en.name: Bridget of Sweden
en.summary: Swedish noblewoman, wife, and mother of eight who, widowed, founded a religious order and became one of medieval Europe's most influential mystics.
en.body: Bridget was married at thirteen to a Swedish nobleman, and the couple had eight children together and lived what by all accounts was a devout and happy marriage before his death sent her into a period of intense mourning that gave way to a call to religious life. She founded the Bridgettine Order, notable for its double monasteries housing both monks and nuns under an abbess's authority, and she traveled to Rome, where she spent the rest of her life urging popes then residing in Avignon to return to Rome and pressing for Church reform. Her extensively recorded visions, compiled as the Revelations, were hugely influential in medieval spirituality and remain a major source for private devotional literature on Christ's Passion. She died in Rome in 1373, and her efforts are credited as one of the pressures that eventually brought the papacy back to Rome. She was canonized in 1391 and is a patron saint of Europe.
